prompt: Write a note to a friend about a funny thing that happened with a neighbor. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the note only.
final_message:
Hey Sam,

I have to tell you what happened with Gary next door, because I'm still laughing about it.

You know how he's been obsessed with his lawn since spring? He's out there at 7 a.m. with a little measuring tape, I swear. Anyway, last Saturday I was on the porch with my coffee, and I noticed a package on my doorstep. It was addressed to him, so I figured I'd be a good neighbor and carry it over.

I knock. No answer. But I can hear him in the backyard, muttering, so I walk around the side gate. And there is Gary, standing perfectly still in the middle of his lawn, holding a garden hose, staring at a sprinkler head that has clearly lost its mind. It was shooting water sideways, straight up, and in a weird little spiral, like a fountain at a casino.

"Don't," he says, without turning around. "Don't say anything."

I said nothing. I just held up the package like a waiter presenting a bottle of wine.

He sighs and tells me it's the replacement sprinkler head. The *third* one. Apparently the first two were the wrong size, and the one he'd just installed was installed upside down. He'd been out there for two hours, getting more and more soaked, and the sprinkler was winning.

So I put the box down and helped him. Meaning I stood there and read the instructions out loud while he crouched in the mud. At one point the sprinkler swung around and hit him square in the face, and I made a noise I can only describe as a goose being startled. He looked at me, dripping, with grass stuck to his forehead, and said very calmly, "I'd like you to know I have a degree in engineering."

I lost it. I had to sit down on his patio steps. He started laughing too, and then neither of us could talk for about a minute.

We did fix it, eventually. Turns out you have to turn the water off first. Revolutionary, I know. Now he's got a perfect, gentle little arc of water, and he's weirdly proud of it. He even invited me over for a beer to "admire the results."

I went, obviously. The lawn looks great. I did not mention the goose noise again, but I think it's going to come up at the next block party.

Come visit soon and I'll make you walk past his yard. Bring a raincoat just in case.

Talk soon,
[name]
